issue.title: Biggest pains

repository.name: mobile
repository.description: :calling: Kiwi.com mobile app written in React Native

issue.body:
## Navigation ❓ 
Our navigation (from JS point of view) is not very developer friendly. It's also complicated because of native team requirements.

Solution: We should wrap the navigation into our own custom wrapper. This will solve the developer friendliness.

## Redux ✅ 
~Redux is hard. In our case, it's also a very big mess. The question is: do we need Redux?~

~Solution: There is new React Context and our state management is not so complicated. Let's try only this and we can, later on, try [Unstated](https://github.com/jamiebuilds/unstated) for example.~

Redux has been completely replaced by React Context. It's still painful because of our internal store structure. However, there are two significant improvements:

- we do not have one huge state store but separated contexts
- we do not use string action names anymore but functions from the context

## Map ❓
There is a lot of bugs on our map. They could be mostly avoided by better design but I would like to replace them with beautiful [Mapbox](https://www.mapbox.com/). Oh and yes - there is Mapbox on Kiwi.com frontend as well.

## Sync/async native code vs. debugging ✅ 
~We currently use sync native methods but there is one big disadvantage: we cannot use freely our debug tools.~

We now use only async methods. See below...

## Playground needs improvements 👨‍💻 
I still think that Playground is a great concept but it's not super DX friendly. We should work on it.

## Async `AdaptableLayout` workaround 👨‍💻
We are currently workarounding RN limitation because of iOS multitasking. Would be great to have a better solution (read not a workaround). See: https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/16152

issue.title: Adding option for grids relative to parent grids

repository.name: react-native-responsive-layout
repository.description: Easy way to implement responsive layouts and grids.

issue.body:
This is a workaround for React Native bug where window dimensions would report wrong values when app is used in split screen mode.

https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/16152

By adding `relativeTo='parent'` prop option, root grid can be made relative to `self` and nested grids can be made relative to `parent` allowing all of them to calculate their size class based on width and height of root grid.

issue.title: Calculate Correct Window Dimensions for iOS

labels.name: CLA Signed
labels.description: This label is managed by the Facebook bot. Authors need to sign the CLA before a PR can be reviewed.

repository.name: react-native
repository.description: A framework for building native applications using React

issue.body:
Fixes: #16152

## Changelog:

[iOS] [Fixed] - Pass back correct dimensions for application window in Dimensions module


Test Plan:
----------
Before:
On iOS, when using `Dimensions.get()` for either screen or window, the same value for width and height would be passed back for both screen and window. These values both represent the width and height of the whole screen regardless of the size of the window.

This behavior was similar for listening to the Dimension change event. The even would fire for orientation changes, but would not fire for changes to the window size (e.g. split view app resizing).

After:
On iOS, when the Dimensions module passes back dimensions for the screen, it uses the full screen dimensions. For window, it now uses just the dimensions of the window. This goes back to Objective C and uses `RCTKeyWindow`.

For event handling, the code watches for the application to become active (`UIApplicationDidBecomeActiveNotification`) and then recalculates the window dimensions, compares it to the previous dimensions, and sends a change event if there was a change.

For testing, I threw together a project. I pointed it to a branch on my forked version of react-native.
https://github.com/rdonnelly/WindowVsScreenRN

Please feel free to let me know if anything needs re-working.
